deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a list of elementary operations on the objects of a category written SCD^+. From the surrounding pages, these objects are triples (X, Σ, R). X is a compact surface. Σ is a closed 1-submanifold (circles used for gluing, or boundary circles). R ⊂ Σ is a finite set of marked points. r(c) is the number of marked points on a circle c, and on the next page the marked points of a circle a form a torsor under Z_a/r(a), where Z_a is Z twisted by the orientation ω(a).

The operation here was first titled 'weakening of a marking', which is struck out. It is then treated as a 'surmarquage' (refinement of the marking).

1. Let A^+ be the set of 'effectively marked' circles, i.e. those with r(c) > 0. These are the components C ∈ π0(Σ) with C ∩ R ≠ ∅.
2. Let Σ^+ be their union and B^+ the set of connected components of Σ^+ minus R. Each element of B^+ is an open interval.
3. A refinement is given by a map r': B^+ → N. It consists in inserting r'(b) new subdivision points (first written 'ramification points', corrected to 'subdivision') on each open arc b.
4. Grothendieck notes that this time the construction involves arbitrary choices. Nevertheless the resulting object (X, Σ, R_1) of SCD^+ is well defined up to unique isomorphism. It comes with the marked subset R' = R_1 \ R of new points, and forgetting R' gives back (X, Σ, R).

The restriction to effectively marked circles is what makes 'unique isomorphism' work. On a circle with no marked point, adding points is still possible up to isotopy, but rotations would give non-unique isomorphisms. On an interval between two existing marks, the configuration of k new points is contractible, so it is canonical.

Purpose: this is part of building the 'Teichmüller tower', a modular groupoid of surfaces with boundary data. It needs generating operations: gluing, capping holes by cones ('gommage', previous page), and forgetting or refining marks. These give functors between Teichmüller groupoids. The next page reinterprets uniform refinements as change of the structure group Z/r → Z/(d·r) on the torsors of marked points.
errors: No mathematical error. The uniqueness-up-to-unique-isomorphism claim is implicitly up to isotopy, i.e. at the level of the groupoid; it is not literally true for diffeomorphisms.

The struck title ('affaiblissement') against the actual content (adding points) shows the direction of the operation was still in flux. On the next page Grothendieck notes that restriction versus extension of the operator groups corresponds to weakening versus strengthening of structure, and the direction is reversed for uniform subgeometries.

ideas.what: Category of surfaces with marked circles and finite sets of marked points on them, with operations (gluing, capping, forgetting or adding marks) generating functors between modular groupoids
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller tower / modular groupoid of bordered surfaces with marked boundary points
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower), in outline only

ideas.what: Refining the marking: insert r'(b) new points on each open arc between existing marks; the result is canonical up to unique isomorphism only on circles already carrying a mark
ideas.modern_name: Adding marked boundary points (forgetful maps between moduli or Teichmüller spaces of bordered surfaces with boundary marked points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used systematically in cluster theory (Fomin–Shapiro–Thurston 2008) and topological Fukaya categories (Haiden–Katzarkov–Kontsevich)

ideas.what: Marked points on a circle viewed as a torsor under Z/r(a) twisted by orientation; refinement as change of structure group (from the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Cyclic torsor / framing of boundary components

missed.claim: Grothendieck's SCD^+ objects (surfaces with marked circles carrying finite cyclically ordered point sets), with refinement and forgetting operations, anticipate the 'marked bordered surfaces' later central to cluster algebras and to topological Fukaya categories, where adding boundary marked points induces functors. No link to Grothendieck's 1983 framework appears in that literature.
missed.quote: un surmarquage est défini par la donnée d'une application B^+ → N ... r'(b) nouveaux sommets de subdivision
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows the boundary-marked-point formalism was present in the Teichmüller tower programme a quarter century earlier. The construction itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine definition of an elementary operation within the unpublished SCD^+ formalism. The only notable point is the observation about uniqueness up to unique isomorphism requiring already-marked circles. It is historically interesting as a precursor of the boundary-marked-point formalism, but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: The title should likely read 'Opération de surmarquage' ('sur' inserted above 'marquage'); 'affaiblissement d'un' is struck out.
'dist[?] tels que r(c)>0' is probably 'c.à.d. tels que r(c)>0'.
Struck '(ramification)' replaced by 'subdivision' is correct; 'points' struck and replaced by '(ouverts)' refers to the open arcs.
'défini à isom unique près' refers to the resulting object (X, Σ, R_1); R' ⊂ R_1 is the set of new points, and 'oubli de R'' recovers (X, Σ, R).
